item.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic non 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.35941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the minimal faithful Alt(6)-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful Alt(n)- and Sym(n)-modules with an additive dimension
item.dc:creator: German Mata Gutiez

item.title: The Andreadakis conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.36302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $\gamma_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/\gamma_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We disprove this conjecture for every $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: C. E. Kofinas

item.title: Degree-one cohomology of metacyclic $2$-groups: a low-bit dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.36401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the subalgebra generated by degree-one mod-$2$ cohomology for metacyclic $2$-groups $G=\langle a,b\mid a^{2^\alpha}=1,\ b^{2^m}=a^c,\ b^{-1}ab=a^r\rangle$ with unique normal forms, where $\alpha,m\ge2$ and $r\equiv-1\pmod4$. Presentation compatibility forces $c=0$ or $2^{\alpha-1}$ and $G^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong C_2\times C_{2^m}$. If $c\equiv0\pmod4$, the degree-one-generated algebra is $\mathbb{F}_2 [x,y]/(y^2,x^2+xy)$, a four-dimensional algebra shared by the four nonmodular types of Aaboun--Zekhnini. The unique exceptional case $\alpha=2$, $c=2$ is modular and has infinite-dimensional degree-one algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y]/(y^2,x^2y)$. The regular algebra is PBW, Koszul, universally Koszul, and strongly Koszul, whereas the modular algebra is not Koszul. We realize the regular algebra by inflation from the common quotient $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_4$ and identify its quadratic dual with the characteristic-two Jordan plane. For the inversion tower $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_{2^m}$, we give uniform presentations of the full mod-$2$ cohomology rings and determine the kernels and images of inflation in every degree. Their direct limit yields the continuous cohomology ring of $C_4\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z_2$. We also record an arithmetic consequence for Galois groups arising over cyclotomic $\mathbb Z_2$-extensions of real quadratic fields.
item.dc:creator: Marina Palaisti

item.title: Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.36497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $\Gamma_2$ we construct an explicit representation $\rho:\Gamma_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $\Gamma_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $\Gamma_g$ with $g\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Wu

item.title: On $\pi$-nilpotencies of finite skew braces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\pi$ be a set of primes. We extend the theory of left and right $\pi$-nilpotency in skew braces beyond the nilpotent type setting, and introduce the study of central $\pi$-nilpotency for finite skew braces. We investigate the relationships between these three notions, and a characterisation of central $\pi$-nilpotency in terms of chief factors is also established. This leads to the introduction of the $\pi$-Fitting ideal of a skew brace, for which we prove a local analogue of Fitting's theorem and provide a description in terms of centralisers of chief factors. Finally, we introduce the $\pi$-core of a skew brace and investigate its relationship with $\pi$-ideals and central $\pi$-nilpotency.
item.dc:creator: L. Gong, M. Damele, V. P\'erez-Calabuig, A. Rodr\'iguez-Dur\`a

item.title: Irrationality of the conjugacy growth on Heisenberg groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.37334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that the conjugacy growth series for the Heisenberg groups $H_n(\mathbb{Z})$ is never algebraic, irrespective of the generating set. This makes progress towards the conjecture that all finitely presented groups that are not virtually abelian have irrational conjugacy growth series. Contrary to the group $H_3(\mathbb{Z})$, where the conjugacy growth is $n^2\log(n)$, the conjugacy growth of the other Heisenberg groups is polynomial, making these groups the first known nilpotent groups where the irrationality does not follow from the asymptotic growth.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Vandeputte

item.title: Representation and abelianization growth, particularly along expanding sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.37399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two obstructions to a finite group $G$ having a generating $d$-tuple whose Cayley graph has spectral gap at least $\epsilon$. Lubotzky and Weiss proved that such a gap forces $\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, the largest order of the abelianization of a subgroup of index at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk))$, while de la Harpe, Robertson and Valette proved that it forces $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)$, the number of irreducible complex representations of degree at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_\epsilon(dk^2))$. We show that the first bound implies the second, and in fact implies it with $k^2$ replaced by $k\log k$. For this, we prove that every finite $d$-generated group satisfies the inequality $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)\leq\exp((d-1)k\log k+O(dk))\cdot\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, regardless of its spectral gap. The leading term $(d-1)k\log k$ is attained by powers of alternating groups, and it disappears for groups without large alternating sections. The proof reduces to counting the finite primitive subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbf{C})$, and we show that there are at most $\exp(O(\log^4m))$ of them up to conjugacy and scalars. Wigderson asked whether $k^2$ in the second bound can be lowered to $k$, so our result answers his question up to a logarithm. We do not know whether the logarithm is actually needed. For powers of alternating groups, the natural candidates, we show that a spectral gap keeps the number of factors a fixed power below the maximum allowed by $d$-generation, and that random generators have spectral gap tending to $0$ already for superpolynomially many factors.
item.dc:creator: Urban Jezernik

item.title: On a problem of A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov concerning $S_n$-closed subformations of a one-generated formation
item.description: arXiv:2610.37462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Throughout this paper, all groups are finite. Let $\mathrm{form}(G)$ denote the formation generated by a group $G$. A formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is said to be $S_n$-closed if every subnormal subgroup of every group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{F}$. A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov posed the problem of proving that $\mathrm{form}(G)$ has only finitely many $S_n$-closed subformations for every group $G$ (Problem 14.81 of the Kourovka Notebook). In this paper we propose a negative answer to this problem. We prove that for the group $G_0=(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)\times\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ of order 28800, where $C_2$ acts on $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ by an outer automorphism, the formation $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ has an infinite strictly descending chain of $S_n$-closed subformations. The main tool is a family of central-valued multilinear maps, defined for every group in $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ by its outer actions on its components; their vanishing is preserved under taking epimorphic images, subdirect products and subnormal subgroups. The members of the chain are separated by central quotients of the groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)^{2^d-1}\rtimes C_2^d$, $d\geq 2$. Using Burichenko's description of the lattice of subformations of $\mathrm{form}(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)$, we also prove that every non-empty $S_n$-closed subformation of $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ is generated, as an ordinary formation, by a single group, and that the set of such subformations is countably infinite. Finally, we determine the intersection of the chain and give an explicit generator of it.
item.dc:creator: Chenxiao Lin

item.title: Algebraic fiberings of right-angled Coxeter groups on bipartite cone graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.37641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study systems of moves and states in the sense of [JNW21] on certain bipartite graphs, and the associated homomorphisms from the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups to $\mathbb Z$. We give examples of right-angled Coxeter groups whose graphs do not satisfy the legal system criterion, but contain finite index right-angled Coxeter subgroups whose graphs admit legal systems. We also provide a family of examples of graphs without legal systems, where no sequence of the considered graph operations yields a graph with a legal system. Moreover, we show that for a bipartite graph and an orbit of non-empty states under the bipartite system of moves, the associated homomorphism from the commutator subgroup of the right-angled Coxeter group to $\mathbb Z$ has finitely generated kernel if and only if the system is legal.
item.dc:creator: Kasia Jankiewicz, Shayan Miri

item.title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Hao Yu, Tianlei Zhou

item.title: A new infinite family of covers of complete graphs that admit a half-transitive action of a Suzuki simple group
item.description: arXiv:2610.36165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a new infinite family of antipodal $2(q-1)$-covers of complete graphs $K_{q^2+1}$ of diameter $3$, where $q=2^{2e+1}\ge 8$, admitting a half-transitive action of the Suzuki simple group $Sz(q)$. We further show that each constructed cover admits an involutory automorphism interchanging the two $Sz(q)$-orbits on arcs, which yields that its full automorphism group is arc-transitive.
item.dc:creator: Ludmila Yu. Tsiovkina

item.title: Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.
item.dc:creator: Lihuang Ding, Abdul Zalloum

item.title: Filling knots and essential geodesic systole
item.description: arXiv:2610.36259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023]. This answers two questions of Biringer.
item.dc:creator: Christopher J. Leininger, Yandi Wu

item.title: Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings
item.description: arXiv:2610.36394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Saul D. Freedman, Melissa Lee, Dragan Maru\v{s}i\v{c}, Toma\v{z} Pisanski

item.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.37291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.
item.dc:creator: Li Luo, Rui Song, Yang Yang

item.title: Rank functions, $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions and class numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.37490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: If $F$ is a number field and $F = F_0 \subset F_1 \subset F_2\subset \cdots$ is a tower of Galois extensions with $\mathrm{Gal}(F_n/F)$ cyclic of order $p^n$, K. Iwasawa gave a closed formula for the growth of the $p$-part of the class number of $F_n$ whenever $n$ is large enough. We present a new proof of this formula, obtained by reinterpreting its summands in terms of Sylvester matrix rank functions on the Iwasawa algebra $\Lambda$ without resorting to the classification of finitely-generated $\Lambda$-modules up to pseudo-isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Iq Souza

item.title: The double coset problem for parabolic subgroups of braid groups
item.description: arXiv:1402.5541v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the double coset problem for arbitrary parabolic subgroups of the $n$-strand braid group $B_n$, by reducing it to the simultaneous conjugacy problem in the larger group $B_{n+1}$. The resulting decision algorithm is uniform in the braid index and the supplied subgroup generators. We also formulate the reduction for general group embeddings, and apply it to additional commuting constraints, several other spherical Artin types, and finite direct products.
item.dc:creator: Arkadius Kalka, Mina Teicher, Boaz Tsaban

item.title: Actions of acylindrically hyperbolic groups on $\ell^1$
item.description: arXiv:2309.12915v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct explicit affine uniformly Lipschitz actions on $\ell^1$ for certain groups with hyperbolic features. For acylindrically hyperbolic groups, our actions have unbounded orbits, while for residually finite hyperbolic groups and for mapping class groups, the actions have proper orbits, with the induced $\ell^1$-metric quasi-isometric (respectively, almost quasi-isometric, up to a logarithmic factor) to the word metric. This allows us to construct proper continuous affine uniformly Lipschitz actions on $L^1$, with undistorted orbits, for all simple groups of real rank one.
item.dc:creator: Cornelia Drutu, John M. Mackay

item.title: Terminal Geometry of Rank-Two Nielsen Reduction on Simplicial Trees
item.description: arXiv:2512.00957v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a locally finite simplicial tree, and let $\Gamma=\langle\gamma_1,\gamma_2\rangle\leq\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ be a discrete subgroup generated by hyperbolic automorphisms acting without inversions, whose axes have finite edge intersection. We locate explicitly, using the Euclidean algorithm, the first stopping state of rank-two Nielsen reduction and determine the exact characteristic-set geometry of its terminal Nielsen pair. Write $m_1\geq m_2>0$ for the normalized translation lengths, $l$ for the axis-overlap length, and $d=\gcd(m_1,m_2)$. If $l=0$, the initial pair satisfies the Schottky criterion. If $l>0$, Euclidean quotients and remainders partition $0<l\leq m_1+m_2-d$ into intervals locating the first stopping state and its ordered Nielsen generators. Interior points yield terminal Schottky pairs. At nonfinal right endpoints, an auxiliary translated-axis overlap $l_0$ distinguishes Schottky terminal pairs from pairs containing a nontrivial elliptic generator. At the final endpoint and for larger overlaps, a nontrivial elliptic terminal generator occurs. We compute the terminal translation lengths and the relative geometry of axes or fixed subtrees in every case. Each terminal pair is Nielsen-equivalent to the initial pair and generates $\Gamma$. If both terminal generators are hyperbolic, they form a Schottky pair; otherwise exactly one is nontrivial elliptic. By local finiteness and discreteness, this element has finite order, so $\Gamma$ contains nontrivial torsion and is not free of rank two.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du, Sa'ar Hersonsky

item.title: Matrix Waring Problem-III
item.description: arXiv:2610.17698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n,k$ be positive integers and $q$ be a prime power. We prove that there exists a real constant $C_k$ depending only on $k$ such that if $ \# M_n(\mathbb{F}_q) > C_k$ then every element in $M_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is a sum of two $k$th powers, proving Larsen's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Kishore, Sunil Kumar Mallick

item.title: Filling Links and Essential Systole
item.description: arXiv:2505.00896v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We answer a question of Freedman and Krushkal, producing filling links in any closed, orientable 3-manifold. The links we construct are hyperbolic, and have large essential systole, contrasting earlier geometric constraints on hyperbolic links in 3-manifolds due to Adams-Reid and Lakeland-Leininger.
item.dc:creator: Christopher J. Leininger, Yandi Wu

item.title: Dehn quandles of surfaces and their bounded cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2602.17661v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce new families of quandles associated with closed orientable surfaces that can distinguish surfaces up to homeomorphism. These quandles generalize the classical Dehn quandle and are defined, respectively, on isotopy classes of unoriented essential closed curves and on integral weighted multicurves. We establish their fundamental algebraic properties and construct a natural quandle covering relating the two families. We further investigate their large-scale geometry and prove that they are unbounded with respect to the quandle metric. We determine their second bounded quandle cohomology and show that its dimension equals the cardinality of the continuum. We also establish a quandle-theoretic analogue of the Gromov Mapping Theorem, showing that the natural projection from an abelian quandle extension onto its base quandle induces an injection on bounded quandle cohomology in every degree. Finally, motivated by recent developments in quandle algebras, we study idempotents in the integral quandle algebras associated with the classical Dehn quandle. In particular, we prove that the integral quandle algebra of the Dehn quandle of the torus admits no non-trivial idempotents.
item.dc:creator: Pankaj Kapari, Deepanshi Saraf, Mahender Singh

item.title: Compactifications of Abelian Group Bundles and a Topological Halmos--von Neumann-type Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2608.28335v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The topological Halmos--von Neumann theorem is a fundamental result of topological dynamics that completely classifies continuous actions of abelian topological groups which are ergodic and have discrete spectrum. It rests on a correspondence between such actions (up to the choice of a distinguished point), compactifications of the acting group and subgroups of its dual group. We generalize both the classical statement and the underlying categorical equivalences to the framework of open group bundles over locally compact base spaces. As a byproduct, we establish a Pontryagin-type duality between \'etale Hausdorff abelian group bundles and open proper Hausdorff abelian group bundles, extending the classical duality between discrete and compact abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Anglewitz, Patrick Hermle, Henrik Kreidler
